messages:
jordan_support: Heads up — customer ACCT-412 reports a regression after this morning's canary -> prod rollout. Small prompt template changes (extra space / newline) now produce wrong JSON output and occasional hallucinations. Posting details.

jordan_support: Customer says their templates used to be tolerant of trailing whitespace and `\n` tokens. After the rollout, outputs sometimes drop fields or add random text. They provided repro and request IDs.

jordan_support: Repro steps from customer (copied):
```
POST /v1/generate
{
  "model": "redwood-v1.3.0",
  "input_template": "Order summary:\nCustomer: {{name}}\nItems:\n{{items}}\nTotal: ${{total}}\n",
  "variables": {"name":"Acme","items":"- widget x1","total":"12.00"}
}
```
Result used to be a tidy JSON block. Now they sometimes get: `\n{"customer":"Acme" some random text...` or missing Total field.

mike_oncall: :eyes: Any deploy metadata? Which variant rolled? I saw canary -> 2026-03-12 09:11 UTC rollout for v1.3.0 with tokenizer hotfix. deploy-bot, did the change include tokenization changes? 

deploy-bot: Canary promotion event: deploy 2026-03-12T09:11:32Z. Changes: model packaging, tokenizer alignment to unify whitespace normalization (PR #8721). No automatic rollback.

elaine_ml: pinging @mike_oncall and @sam_backend. The tokenizer alignment PR intentionally changed how trailing whitespace is normalized for speed — could be an off-by-one in token offsets for sequence-boundary templates.

sam_backend: If token offsets shifted, prompt-parsing code that relies on exact byte offsets for template injections might break. But we don't use byte offsets anywhere intentionally — unless some legacy templating path uses naive substring insertion. I'll look at the templating service logs.

jordan_support: Customer provided request ids: req_0a9f3c, req_0a9f4b. They said it started between 09:20 and 09:40 UTC.

sam_backend: Pulling logs for req_0a9f3c... snippet:
```
2026-03-12T09:22:11Z INFO template_rendering id=req_0a9f3c template_len=74 variables_injected=3 mode=legacy_inject
2026-03-12T09:22:11Z DEBUG rendered_prompt="Order summary:\nCustomer: Acme\nItems:\n- widget x1\nTotal: $12.00\n"
2026-03-12T09:22:11Z DEBUG runtime_tokens=[23,45,12,...]
2026-03-12T09:22:12Z WARN model_output_mismatch id=req_0a9f3c parsed_json_missing_keys=["total"]
```

elaine_ml: The templates show `mode=legacy_inject` — that's our older path that does string-level concatenation. We shipped a tokenizer alignment that changed tokenization for trailing newlines; legacy_inject relies on prior tokenization to decide whether to append an extra space. That could explain missing fields if the model sees a different context boundary.

mike_oncall: Repro locally with v1.3.0 image? @elaine_ml can you run the injection path with both old and new tokenizer and diff the generated token ids? Also check micro-batching behavior — we saw slight differences in batch tokenization ordering in PR notes.

elaine_ml: Will do. Quick check: I ran two local runs (tokenizer v1.2.8 vs v1.3.0) against the customer's template. Diff shows token stream diverges at trailing newline: v1.2.8 tokens [ ... , 1024] vs v1.3.0 [ ... , 1024, 0] (0=EOS placeholder). That extra token increases the apparent context length and moves expected generation boundary by 1.

sam_backend: If the injection code was computing insert_point = len(tokens)-1 and then truncating output_by_tokens, that off-by-one could trim the last fields. We should audit legacy_inject logic.

jordan_support: Customer is asking for an ETA and whether we can patch or roll back. They are blocking a launch.

mike_oncall: Immediate options:
- Hotfix: Adjust legacy_inject to use semantic boundary detection rather than raw token count (fast, low-risk).
- Rollback: Revert tokenizer alignment across prod (higher risk, affects other customers and performance).
- Workaround: Suggest customer modify templates to remove trailing newline or add explicit sentinel token (e.g., "<END>") — but they'd rather not.

elaine_ml: I can prepare a minimal patch to legacy_inject that normalizes whitespace before token-count compare. That should restore previous behavior and is small. Will run unit tests and can cut a canary in ~90 minutes.

sam_backend: I'll prepare a hotfix branch and add targeted integration test using the customer's template. Also add a regression test for whitespace normalization.

deploy-bot: Hotfix branch created: hotfix/legacy-inject-token-boundary. CI pending.

mike_oncall: Also, let's surface this in the release notes and ops runbook: changes to tokenizer may affect template-based injection paths. Need a postmortem after fix.

jordan_support: Customer wants a temporary mitigation they can apply themselves. Any minimal template edit they can do quickly? 

elaine_ml: Short-term mitigation: append an explicit sentinel string to the template, e.g., add "\n<END>" after Total line and add to variables. That prevents ambiguity. Example:
```
"input_template": "Order summary:\nCustomer: {{name}}\nItems:\n{{items}}\nTotal: ${{total}}\n<END>"
```
This will be robust across tokenizer variants.

mike_oncall: Good. Send that to the customer as an immediate workaround while we rollout hotfix.

jordan_support: Sent workaround to customer at 09:45 UTC; they replied: "works, thanks — but we need permanent fix." Marking high priority.

deploy-bot: CI passed for hotfix, canary build ready. Canary window request: 10:30 UTC for 15m.

mike_oncall: Approving canary. @sam_backend coordinate canary metrics (parse-error-rate, customer-templates-failure-rate) and alert if >1% delta.

sam_backend: Canary started at 10:30. Metrics tracking now. Pulling canary logs for same templates.

sam_backend: Canary logs show legacy_inject normalized whitespace and parsed correctly for the test requests. parse-error-rate dropped from 4.2% to 0.3% for the sampled customers during canary.

elaine_ml: Model output diff looks clean. No added latency. Running extended tests to be safe.

deploy-bot: Canary success at 10:47. Promotion to prod scheduled.

mike_oncall: Rolling to prod now. Watch SLOs. If any regression within next 30m, we rollback.

sam_backend: Prod rollout completed at 11:05. parse-error-rate returned to baseline ~0.2%.

jordan_support: Customer confirmed at 11:12: "Thanks, permanent fix confirmed, templates back to normal." They asked for a note when the postmortem is ready.

mike_oncall: Postmortem assigned to @elaine_ml and @sam_backend. Initial summary: Tokenizer alignment change introduced an extra EOS placeholder token in certain trailing-whitespace cases, exposing bug in legacy_inject truncation logic. Remediation: hotfix normalization + regression tests; long-term: deprecate legacy_inject path and migrate templating to canonical insertion API.

elaine_ml: I'll draft postmortem and include timeline, root cause, remediation, tests, and customer communication. ETA EOD today.

jordan_support: Closing the urgent thread, tagging customer as resolved. Leaving this thread for postmortem comments.

ops-bot: Incident closed: INC-2026-0312-01. Severity: high -> resolved. Recorded on-call: @mike_oncall.
